The user is asking about a simple random sample of 400 windows, labeled in CSV. What they want to know is whether there's a part of the map that can be trusted to have an error rate of at most 5% — this is certification via olmoearth_certify_zone. However, certify_zone requires a design='random' plan (design_path from olmoearth_plan_label_sample) and its labels.

The file names suggest a design: "H5/design_scores_39fe40be_random_400_s11.json" and the "_to_label.csv". These look like outputs of olmoearth_plan_label_sample with design='random'. The scores JSON under OLMOEARTH_SCORES_ROOT (the H5 directory). So we may already have design_path = H5/design_scores_39fe40be_random_400_s11.json? Actually plan_label_sample saves the design and lists windows; the naming pattern "design_scores_<hash>_random_400_s<seed>.json" suggests the design path. And "_to_label.csv" is the CSV to fill in, and the user has filled it in (labeled).

So the flow: olmoearth_estimate_map_error(design_path, labels_path or wrong), then olmoearth_certify_zone(design_path, alpha=0.05) using labels. But do I need the contents of the wrong array? estimate_map_error needs either design_path + wrong, or labels_path. The user says the labels are in the CSV — so I can use labels_path.

2. Call olmoearth_certify_zone(design_path, alpha=0.05, labels_path?) — actually certify_zone's parameters are: design_path, alpha required; wrong or labels_path optional; delta default 0.1, rule default 'prefix'. Since the labels are in the CSV, pass labels_path.

facts.sentence: The map's error rate is estimated at 19.2% (95% interval 15.6% to 23.4%) from 400 labelled windows of a population of 15813; method: exact hypergeometric interval (simple random sample of a finite map).

Ranked by user's accuracy (of the windows the map puts in a class, the share the labels agree with) over the 5 classes with at least 5 map-labelled windows, the lowest are class 5 (0 of 17 correct; 0.0%, 95% interval 0.0% to 19.1%), class 6 (28 of 64 correct; 43.8%, 95% interval 31.6% to 56.5%) and class 1 (7 of 16 correct; 43.8%, 95% interval 20.1% to 69.7%). Classes 0, 2 and 8 have fewer than 5 map-labelled windows (0, 2 and 0), too few to rank.

forbidden_claims.why: a random design makes a certified zone possible, never certain: olmoearth_certify_zone certifies a zone only where the labels drawn in it hold few enough errors for its exact test, so it may certify none, and no design, sample size, budget or plan can promise a certified (or 'certifiable') region, or a zone of any size; these labels certify a zone only if olmoearth_certify_zone, at an alpha the map's use requires, finds one, and it may find none

result.note: no zone certified at alpha=0.05, delta=0.1 with 400 labels; the smallest testable zone (15% of the map) held 63 labels with 5 wrong
result.verdict: No zone is certified at alpha=0.05, delta=0.1 under rule 'prefix': no share of the map is shown to be wrong at most alpha=0.05 of the time.

levels_tested.how_the_rule_tests_them: prefix tests the 18 levels at delta = 0.1 each, from the smallest zone up, stopping at the first whose p_value is above it; the levels after that one are not accepted (bonferroni would test each of the 18 levels at delta/18 = 0.1/18 = 0.00555556)
levels_tested.why_these_levels: a zone must hold at least 45 labels to be certified at alpha=0.05, delta=0.1 (min_labels_to_certify), so with 400 labels no zone below coverage c_min = 0.1125 is tested; another alpha tests other levels

result.reading_levels: Each level's upper_bound is that zone's own bound at delta, before the rule is applied. A level whose upper_bound is below alpha, this alpha or any other, is not thereby certified: certification is the package's exact test under the chosen rule (levels_tested says how this rule tested which levels), and which levels are tested depends on alpha. Only a level marked accepted at this call's alpha is certified. Another alpha tests other levels, so this output says nothing about it; and the guarantee holds for an alpha fixed before the labels were seen, so trying looser alphas until one certifies is not covered by it.
result.design_requirement: Certification needs design='random' (a simple random sample of the map); olmoearth_certify_zone refuses a 'confidence' or 'proportional' design, so recommend only a random design for a certified zone. A random design makes a certified zone possible, not certain: olmoearth_certify_zone may certify nothing.
next_steps: Label more windows under a NEW random design fixed in advance: olmoearth_plan_label_sample with design='random' and a larger budget, with alpha, delta and rule set before any of its labels is seen. A random design makes a certified zone possible, not certain: olmoearth_certify_zone may certify nothing.

Not a looser alpha and not another rule on these labels: either is chosen after seeing this result, which the guarantee does not cover (forbidden_claims).

facts.sentence: The map's error rate is estimated at 19.2% (95% interval 15.6% to 23.4%) from 400 labelled windows of a population of 15813; method: exact hypergeometric interval (simple random sample of a finite map). It is the estimate for the whole population from the same labels, not a certification.

forbidden_claims.why: alpha=0.05 was fixed for this call; the guarantee holds only for an alpha fixed before the labels were seen. Proposing or evaluating another alpha after seeing these bounds (e.g. that a looser alpha would certify some share of the map) is not a certification: another alpha tests other levels, a level whose upper_bound is below an alpha is not thereby accepted, and trying alphas until one certifies is not covered

the rule ('prefix' here) is fixed with alpha before the labels are seen; re-running certification under another rule after this one certified nothing is a second look that the guarantee does not cover; prefix accepts levels from the smallest zone upward while p_value <= delta = 0.1 and stops at the first failure (the smallest zone's p_value is 0.907); bonferroni accepts any level with p_value <= delta/18 = 0.00556 (the smallest p_value of the 18 levels tested is 0.779), so no level passes under either rule

a random design makes a certified zone possible, never certain: olmoearth_certify_zone certifies a zone only where the labels drawn in it hold few enough errors for its exact test, so it may certify none, and no design, sample size, budget or plan can promise a certified (or 'certifiable') region, or a zone of any size; this random design of 400 labels certified nothing at alpha=0.05, and a new one with a larger budget may certify nothing either

Response: No certified zone at alpha=0.05, delta=0.1. Instead, what can be said is the whole-map estimate: 19.2% error rate, 95% interval 15.6–23.4%, based on 400 out of 15813 windows, method being the exact hypergeometric distribution interval. Weakest classes by user's accuracy: class 5 (0/17), class 6 (28/64, 43.8%), class 1 (7/16, 43.8%). Classes 4 and 7 are strong (about 95%). content:
**No.** The certification test certified nothing at alpha = 0.05, delta = 0.1 (rule "prefix"): no share of the map — even the smallest testable zone, 15% of the map holding 63 labels with 5 wrong — passed its exact test. So I cannot say any part of this map is wrong at most 5% of the time.

What you *can* say, from the same 400 labels (population 15,813):

| Claim | Value |
|---|---|
| Whole-map error rate | **19.2%** (95% interval **15.6% to 23.4%**) |
| Method | Exact hypergeometric interval, simple random sample of a finite map |
| Best classes (user's accuracy) | class 7: 95.9% (163/170); class 4: 95.4% (125/131) |
| Weakest classes | class 5: 0% (0/17); class 6: 43.8% (28/64); class 1: 43.8% (7/16) |

So the honest statement is: the map as a whole is about 81% accurate, but the strongest-confidence region fails the 5% test — the errors are spread too evenly for a high-confidence core to stand out.

If a certified zone matters for your use, the only clean route is a **new random design with a larger budget**, planned (with alpha and delta fixed) before its labels are seen — I can plan that via `olmoearth_plan_label_sample` when you tell me how many more windows you can label. Note that even then certification may certify nothing; it makes it possible, not certain.
